td2pz0z.latestHeadline: SC directs Centre to form expert panel to regulate unethical pharma marketing
td2pz0z.summary: In early October, the Supreme Court asked the Centre to set up a three-member panel to examine whether drugmakers need legally enforceable rules governing gifts, incentives and other promotional practices. The petition before the court had raised concerns that pharmaceutical companies were allegedly offering doctors expensive gifts, overseas trips and other incentives to encourage them to prescribe particular drugs. The Hindu reported the direction as one for an expert panel to regulate unethical pharma marketing.

tyy55n6.name: AI and cyber fraud regulation
tyy55n6.latestHeadline: AI regulations: Consultation paper in a month; safety, deepfakes among key focus areas, says Vaishnaw
tyy55n6.summary: On 8 October 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, speaking at India Mobile Congress 2026, called for a global mechanism to tackle cross-border cyber fraud and deepfake threats. He also highlighted India's digital governance and its DBT system. The same day, Minister Vaishnaw said the government has always maintained that AI and other technologies cannot be regulated by law alone, and that a techno-legal solution is needed with stakeholders brought on board. The Hindu's report of his remarks said a consultation paper would come in a month, with safety and deepfakes among the key focus areas.

events.headline: ‘Cyber fraud does not respect borders’: PM Modi seeks global mechanism at IMC 2026

tqtn8b9.name: Shipbuilding and maritime self-reliance
tqtn8b9.latestHeadline: Cochin Shipyard gets order to build 40 ships from U.S., Germany, Norway, other nations: Sonowal

events.headline: India aims to be self-reliant in shipping and shipbuilding by 2047: Sonowal
Cochin Shipyard gets order to build 40 ships from U.S., Germany, Norway, other nations: Sonowal

tqtn8b9.summary: On 8 October 2026, Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal said India aims to be self-reliant in shipping and shipbuilding by 2047, and that the government is building an ecosystem to help domestic shipyards win global orders as the country targets a place among the world's top five shipbuilding nations. The same day, The Hindu reported that Cochin Shipyard had received an order to build 40 ships from the U.S., Germany, Norway and other nations, according to Sonowal. A senior Shipping Ministry official also said that some Russian entities had shown interest in building ships in India.

t1jobkuw.name: Cancer drug trade margin cap
t1jobkuw.latestHeadline: Centre to cap trade margins on non-scheduled cancer drugs to 30% of MRP
t1jobkuw.summary: On 8 October 2026, Mint and The Hindu reported that the Centre plans to cap trade margins on non-scheduled cancer drugs at 30% of MRP. The Hindu said the average trade mark-up on these drugs is now around 170%, reaching 700% in some cases. Both outlets reported that the cap could cut retail prices by up to 70%, and The Hindu added that this would bring cumulative annual savings of ₹2,500 crore for patients. Mint described the move as coming ahead of a broader crackdown on steep mark-ups in cancer medicines.

events.headline: Centre plans 30% trade-margin cap on non-scheduled cancer drugs

t116za04.summary: On 8 October, the US suspended Microsoft, Infosys, Wipro, HCL and other tech firms from a labour programme, with the move coming amid the Trump administration's broader focus on prioritising US workers and scrutinising programmes that companies use to employ foreign nationals. On 9 October, Karnataka's IT Minister Priyank Kharge said that US Green Card curbs and tighter mobility conditions could accelerate India's shift to high-value tech work.
